title.en: A salary and a monthly allowance

summary.en: A correction that changes how staff pay is described.

body.en:
In this short Al Maktab taster, Malik says *يحتاجون مصروف شهري*: they need a monthly allowance. His colleague replies *اسمه راتب*: it is called a salary.

*مصروف* is money for spending or expenses. It can describe an allowance. *راتب* is regular pay for work. Her correction matters because she is talking about employees' pay, rather than treating it like pocket money. The two nouns are not interchangeable in every situation.

*شهري* means monthly and is built from the Arabic word for month. In *مصروف شهري*, the adjective follows the noun and takes its masculine singular form. The drawer shows the matching feminine form for use with a feminine singular noun.

The word drawer gives the plurals of the two money nouns and the agreement forms of the monthly adjective. This note keeps its Arabic examples to the short spoken exchange.

The Cairo Arabic Language Academy documents [salary and regularity](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/رتب) and [month and monthly](https://www.arabicacademy.gov.eg/ar/search_engine/roots/شهر). These dictionary connections explain the word families; they do not date the first Saudi use.
